newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cash crude diffs steady late, EFPs easing.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cash crude diffs steady late, EFPs easing.

text.p: U.S. cash crude differentials were steady in modest late-day trading on Wednesday as pressure eased on exchange-for-physical transactions, traders said.
Cash West Texas Intermediate/Cushing gave up the day's earlier gains after Iraq's U.N. Ambassador Nizar Hamdoon told Reuters that the impending re-start of oil-for-food sales was proceeding on track.
July NYMEX settled at $18.53 a barrel, down 14 cents a barrel from Tuesday's close.
July EFPs were trading around 17-19 cents premium, off a couple of pennies from recent days as traders reconciled their positions ahead of the June 20 NYMEX crude contract expiry.
"EFPs are easing a little in the back months," a Gulf Coast trader said. August EFPs were around 10 cents, while July for three months was valued at 10-13 cents a barrel.
West Texas Intermediate/Midland was at WTI/Cushing minus 40-37 cents a barrel, somewhat wider from this morning. Deals were done at minus 38 and 39 cents.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James was at 22-20 cents discount, even with this morning. The grade traded at minus 19, 20, and 21 cents, while Auguust deals were done at minus 14 and 15 cents.
A Gulf Coast trader said LLS failed to strengthen on the narrow transatlantic arbitrage because plenty of the grade was already in storage.
Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire hovered around minus 70-65 cents, while Eugene Island was around minus 2.08-03 cents.
West Texas Sour/Midland stood around $1.68-65 under WTI/Cushing. The grade fetched minus $1.64 and $1.65, traders said.
WTI/Cushing Posting Plus slipped late to $1.75-78 a barrel after trading in the $1.80s earlier.
